claims.text: The ability of CrFeCoNiX alloys to form and maintain a protective oxide scale above 900 °C is primarily controlled by segregation and preferential oxidation of X.
When X is Si, the alloy forms an interfacial Si-enriched oxide.
The oxide formed by the Si-containing alloy may contain a mixture of Cr2O3 and SiO2.
The Si-enriched oxide is chemically and thermally coherent with the substrate.
When X is Mn, less compatible Mn-rich oxidation products are promoted.
When X is Mn or Al, a faster-growing, multilayered oxide system can form.
The Mn- or Al-associated oxide structures generate internal stresses that cause cracking or spallation.
The proposed comparison changes X among Si, Mn, and Al while holding the other alloy constituents and exposure protocol constant.
The Si-containing alloy is expected to develop a chemically homogeneous and interfacially adherent oxide layer.
The Mn- or Al-containing alloys are expected to develop heterogeneous, layered oxide structures.
Mn- or Al-rich oxides may mismatch the alloy substrate in lattice parameters and thermal expansion.
Preferential oxidation of Cr and X controls the nature of the oxide scale.
For X = Si, slow-growing and chemically stable oxides, together with beneficial elemental segregation, promote a coherent and adherent scale.
For X = Mn or Al, rapid and less coherent oxidation produces stresses through thermal-expansion mismatch or phase-transformation volume changes.
Oxidation-induced stresses in the Mn- or Al-containing alloys ultimately cause oxide cracking or spallation.
CrFeCoNiSi will retain a stable, continuous, coherent protective oxide layer during high-temperature exposure.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiAl will form less coherent, rapidly growing oxide layers that tend to crack or spall.
Vacuum exposure produces minimal oxidation and can serve as a baseline for oxidation-independent behavior.
The proposed mechanism applies to single- or multiphase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid solutions exposed above 900 °C under sustained oxidative or corrosive conditions.
Comparable coherent and protective scales in the Mn- or Al-containing alloys, or failure of the Si-containing alloy to form such a scale, would falsify the proposed X-dependent ordering.
